Article 73

Families in efforts to protect women's rights shall play a role in:

a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights in the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades women's dignity.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 29

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The service of providing safe houses as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 25

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the social field;
b. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or existing social community organizations; or
c. religious agencies and/or organizations.

Article 24

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Women victims of acts of violence have the right to free health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. visum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 75

(1) Guidance on women empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:

a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and child victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and child victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent is authorized to conduct guidance in the implementation of women empowerment and child protection.

Article 76

(1) The Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women empowerment and child protection shall submit reports on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77

(1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

(2) In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a Regional Apparatus in accordance with its duties and functions.

(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for women and child protection program policies in the Region.

Article 32

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:

a. women victims of violence can continue their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 6

Subparagraph a

Sufficiently clear

Subparagraph b

What is meant by gender justice is a fair condition and treatment of women and men, so that justice for women and men is realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of their role.

What is meant by gender equality is the equality of conditions and positions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, educational, defense, national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development with balanced impact.

Subparagraph c

What is meant by local wisdom is good cultural values that exist in a community, because every culture teaches certain ways, rules or methods to obtain knowledge or truth about something.

Subparagraph d

Sufficiently clear

Subparagraph e

What is meant by non-discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be refused or given priority over others except on the consideration of certain emergencies.

Subparagraph f

Sufficiently clear

Subparagraph g

Sufficiently clear

Subparagraph h

Sufficiently clear

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Paragraph 3

Social Field

Article 71

(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of women's and children's rights;
b. provide protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provide information from/or report violations of women's and children's rights to the authorities; and
d. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of women's and children's rights.
(2) Family and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of women's and children's rights.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:

(2) Family and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of women's and children's rights.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 53

Article 27

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Self-explanatory

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 73

Families in efforts to protect women's rights shall play a role in:

a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights in the household; and
c. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades women's dignity.

Article 75

(1) Guidance on women empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:

a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and child victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and child victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent is authorized to conduct guidance in the implementation of women empowerment and child protection.

Article 76

(1) The Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women empowerment and child protection shall submit reports on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77

(1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

(2) In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a Regional Apparatus in accordance with its duties and functions.

(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for women and child protection program policies in the Region.

Article 24

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Women victims of acts of violence have the right to free health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. visum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 29

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 25

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the social field;
b. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or existing social community organizations; or
c. religious agencies and/or organizations.

Article 71

(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of women's and children's rights;
b. provide protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provide information from/or report violations of women's and children's rights to the authorities; and
d. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of women's and children's rights.
(2) Family and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of women's and children's rights.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The service of providing safe houses as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 53

(1) The Regional Government must provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from financial burdens for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking.
(3) The Regional Government, community, family and parents must ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 62

(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.

(2) The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices;
b. all work that exploits, provides, or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that exploits, provides, or involves children in the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of children.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Paragraph (1)

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Self-explanatory

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 29

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 21 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Paragraph 2

Legal Field

Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore mental and systematic awareness of differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 30. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 31. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to recognize gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 32. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit homes, children's friendly telephone (TESSA) 129 or other forms. 34. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 35. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 37. Customs are traditional local wisdom values that apply and are still practiced from generation to generation in the community. 38. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinative institution at the regency level that coordinates policy, program and activity efforts to realize a child-friendly regency. 39. Regional Action Plan for Child-Friendly Regency Development is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a Child-Friendly Regency.

Article 75

(1) Guidance on women empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:

a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and child victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and child victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent is authorized to conduct guidance in the implementation of women empowerment and child protection.

Article 76

(1) The Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women empowerment and child protection shall submit reports on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77

(1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

(2) In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a Regional Apparatus in accordance with its duties and functions.

(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for women and child protection program policies in the Region.

Article 24

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Women victims of acts of violence have the right to free health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. visum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 50

(1) Every education unit organizer to children to obtain education services without discrimination.

(2) Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.

(3) In the case where a child victim of violence experiences dropping out of school, the education unit organizer is required to coordinate with related agencies.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The service of providing safe houses as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 71

(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of women's and children's rights;
b. provide protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provide information from/or report violations of women's and children's rights to the authorities; and

(2) Family and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of women's and children's rights.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.
