CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 32

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:

a. women victims of violence can continue their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The service of providing safe houses as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 27

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 27

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Article 29

Article 71

(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of women's and children's rights;
b. provide protection to victims and emergency assistance;
c. provide information from/or report violations of women's and children's rights to the authorities; and
d. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of women's and children's rights.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Self-explanatory

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Paragraph (1)

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring the problems experienced by victims and be able to empower the victims.

Letter b

Self-explanatory

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only by those relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to the victim.

Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of safety and comfort is that service providers must ensure that the victim is in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problem.

Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique, each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism) so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information coming from the victim will not be assessed or judged.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/action to be taken.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using appropriate language understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that the victim is served in a language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more women with disabilities/difable/disable have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those with mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be taken from special school (SLB) teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with the proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same thing related to identity and case narrative.

Letter k

What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood and can openly tell their problem.

Letter l

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Women's empowerment is an effort to empower women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, both in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives both directly and indirectly, which are carried out with the agreement and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thought. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the government, community and business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Abandoned child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition in which the material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens are fulfilled so that they can live decently and be able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The service of providing safe houses as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.

Article 73

Families in efforts to protect women's rights shall play a role in:

a. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs;
b. preventing violations of women's rights in the household; and

Article 71

(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of women's and children's rights;
b. provide protection to victims and emergency assistance;

(2) Family and Parents are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of women's and children's rights.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience acts that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who has control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is the OPD apparatus who has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out witness assistance and/or victim assistance processes for violence against women and children that are gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Transit home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 29.

(1) The Technical Team as referred to in Article 11 letter j consists of apparatus who understand gender-responsive budget analysis.

(2) The regional action plan for regional gender mainstreaming as referred to in Article 11 letter k contains:

a. gender mainstreaming in laws and regulations;
b. gender mainstreaming in the development cycle;
c. strengthening of gender mainstreaming institutions; and

Article 36

(1) In order to improve family quality, the Regional Government is responsible for:

a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and children's rights;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services.
(2) The responsibility of the Regional Government in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 75

(1) Guidance on women empowerment and child protection shall be conducted by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:

a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and child victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and child victims of violence; and
e. improving the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
(3) The Regent is authorized to conduct guidance in the implementation of women empowerment and child protection.

Article 76

(1) The Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women empowerment and child protection shall submit reports on the implementation of women and child protection programs to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically once (1) every 6 (six) months.

Article 77

(1) The Regent shall conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically once (1) every 3 (three) months.

(2) In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint a Regional Apparatus in accordance with its duties and functions.

(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall constitute evaluation material for women and child protection program policies in the Region.

Article 27

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The service of providing safe houses as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 25

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 21 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the social field;
b. Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers or existing social community organizations; or
c. religious agencies and/or organizations.

Article 10

(1) In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of gender mainstreaming, a gender mainstreaming working group is established in all Regional Apparatus.

(2) Members of the gender mainstreaming working group are all heads/leaders of Regional Apparatus.

(3) The Regent designates the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers Government Affairs in the field of Regional Development Planning as the Chair of the gender mainstreaming working group and the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection as the Head of the Secretariat of the gender mainstreaming working group.

(4) The establishment of the gender mainstreaming working group as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by a Regent's Decree.
